 Gold prices down 2% on the day as US CPI rises more than expected
 By  Neils Christensen 
 Published : 13:30 Updated : 13:47 Kitco News The Leading News Source in Precious Metals 
 Kitco NEWS has a diverse team of journalists reporting on the economy, stock markets, commodities, cryptocurrencies, mining and metals with accuracy and objectivity. Our goal is to help people make informed market decisions through in-depth reporting, daily market roundups, interviews with prominent industry figures, comprehensive coverage (often exclusive) of important industry events and analyses of market-affecting developments.
 (Kitco News) - The gold market has been hit with significant selling pressure as persistent inflation pressures are adding to fears that the Federal Reserve could aggressively raise interest rates next month to cool rising consumer prices.
 The Consumer Price Index (CPI) rose by 0.4% last month, following September’s 0.6% increase, the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics announced on Tuesday. The inflation data was hotter than expected, as economists had forecast a 0.3% increase.
 The report also showed that higher energy prices have become further embedded in the broader economy, as core inflation, which strips out energy and food prices, rose more than expected. Core CPI increased 0.3% last month, matching September’s increase. Consensus estimates expected a 0.2% increase.
 Last year’s months-long government shutdown is also coming back to haunt economists, as no annual inflation data was provided.
 “BLS did not collect survey data for October 2025 because of a lapse in appropriations. For most CPI series, BLS could not publish October 2025 indexes. As a result, BLS cannot publish 12-month percent changes for October 2026 for indexes where October 2025 data are unavailable,” the report said.
 The gold market was already struggling ahead of the latest CPI data, as investors reacted to comments from Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller, who expressed support for a potential 50-basis-point rate hike next month.
 Spot gold last traded at $4,054.90 an ounce, down 2% on the day.
